title: Exotic G-Representations and the Composite BU Dimension Gap
description: Formalizes the question of exotic G-representations: representations where a composite cyclic group Z/n has strictly higher equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimension than any prime subgroup. Defines IsExotic(n,d) as buDim(n,d) > max_{p|n,prime} buDim(p,d), proves primes and prime powers are never exotic, shows exotic requires ≥ 2 distinct prime factors, and proves the formula is monotone under divisibility. Under the formula conjecture, no exotic representations exist.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: 5 axioms inherited from parent files: buDim (axiom defining the BU dimension function), buDim_two (classical BU), buDim_prime (Yang-Borsuk for primes), buDim_mono (subgroup monotonicity), buDim_le_formula (open conjecture: buDim ≤ prime formula). The 'not_exotic_prime_pow' and 'no_exotic' results use the formula conjecture axiom.
originalContributions: IsExotic: formal definition of exotic representations where composite group exceeds prime formula
exoticDefect: measure of how much buDim exceeds the prime formula (0 for non-exotic)
not_exotic_prime_pow: prime powers p^k are non-exotic (uses formula axiom; only prime factor is p)
buDimFormula_mono_of_dvd: formula is monotone under divisibility (purely structural, no topology axioms)
exotic_implies_two_prime_factors: exotic requires ≥ 2 distinct prime factors (structural constraint)
conjecture_iff_no_exotic: the formula conjecture is equivalent to absence of all exotic representations

overview.historicalContext: The equivariant Borsuk-Ulam conjecture for composite groups asks whether buDim(n,d) equals the maximum buDim(p,d) over prime divisors p. Smith theory (1941) establishes this for prime powers: buDim(p^k, d) = buDim(p, d), since only the prime subgroup Z/p controls the fixed-point structure. For general composites with multiple prime factors, the question is whether the group structure creates additional topological constraints — 'exotic' representations — beyond what any single prime subgroup exhibits. The Fadell-Husseini ideal-valued cohomological index (1988) is the main tool for attacking the general case, but the conjecture remains open for arbitrary representations.
overview.problemStatement: Are there exotic G-representations: pairs (n, d) where the composite cyclic group Z/n has strictly higher BU dimension than any prime subgroup, i.e., buDim(n, d) > max_{p|n, p prime} buDim(p, d)?
overview.text: Formal analysis of whether composite cyclic groups can create exotic equivariant topology — extra dimensional constraints invisible to any single prime subgroup.
overview.proofStrategy: Define IsExotic(n,d) formally and derive structural constraints: (1) primes can never be exotic (buDimFormula = buDim by definition); (2) prime powers cannot be exotic because their only prime factor gives buDimFormula = buDim(p,d) and the conjecture axiom bounds buDim(p^k,d) ≤ buDim(p,d); (3) exotic must have ≥ 2 distinct prime factors (otherwise it's a prime power case); (4) the formula is monotone under divisibility as a purely combinatorial/structural result. The full answer — that no exotic representations exist — follows from the formula conjecture axiom.
keyInsights: Exotic representations would be exactly the counterexamples to the open conjecture buDim_le_formula
Prime powers are provably non-exotic: buDimFormula(p^k, d) = buDim(p, d) and buDim(p^k, d) ≤ buDim(p, d) by the formula axiom
Exotic requires n to have at least 2 distinct prime factors — the smallest possible candidate is n = 6 = 2 × 3
The formula monotonicity theorem (buDimFormula_mono_of_dvd) follows purely from Nat.primeFactors_mono and Finset.sup_mono — no topology needed
The structural constraint 'exotic implies 2 prime factors' uses only the fact that prime powers are non-exotic, no topological content
prerequisites: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam theory for prime groups (Yang-Borsuk theorem)
BU dimension formula conjecture for composite groups (parent file)
Smith theory for prime power group actions

sections.title: Exotic Representations and Defect
sections.summary: Defines IsExotic(n,d) := buDimFormula(n,d) < buDim(n,d) and exoticDefect(n,d) := buDim(n,d) - buDimFormula(n,d). Proves defect = 0 iff not exotic.
sections.mathContext: IsExotic captures the failure of the formula conjecture for specific (n,d). exoticDefect measures the gap. Since buDimFormula ≤ buDim always holds (lower bound), defect is a valid ℕ subtraction.

sections.title: Non-Exotic Cases: Primes and Prime Powers
sections.summary: Proves primes and prime powers are non-exotic. For primes: buDimFormula(p,d) = buDim(p,d) by definition. For prime powers p^k: only prime factor is p, so buDimFormula(p^k,d) = buDim(p,d), and buDim(p^k,d) ≤ buDim(p,d) by formula axiom.
sections.mathContext: Uses Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow: (p^k).primeFactors = {p} for prime p, k ≠ 0. Then buDimFormula_le + buDim_le_formula give the equality.

sections.title: Formula Monotonicity Under Divisibility
sections.summary: Proves buDimFormula(n,d) ≤ buDimFormula(m,d) when n | m (structural, no axioms). Also states buDim_dvd_mono (n|m → buDim n d ≤ buDim m d).
sections.mathContext: Nat.primeFactors_mono: n|m,m≠0 → primeFactors(n) ⊆ primeFactors(m). Finset.sup_mono packages this into the formula monotonicity.

sections.title: Structural Constraints on Exotic Representations
sections.summary: Proves: exotic → ¬prime (trivial), exotic (with n≥2) → card(primeFactors n) ≥ 2. The two-prime-factors result uses Finset.card_eq_one + Nat.mem_primeFactors.
sections.mathContext: Key argument: if card(primeFactors) = 1, then primeFactors = {p} for some prime p, so n is a prime power → not_exotic_prime_pow contradicts exotic. For n ≥ 2, card ≥ 1 by nonempty_primeFactors.

sections.title: Equivalences with the Conjecture
sections.summary: Proves: IsExotic ↔ ¬(buDim ≤ buDimFormula). Under conjecture: no exotic for n ≥ 2. Conjecture ↔ no exotic for all n ≥ 2.
sections.mathContext: Direct logical reformulations. The conjecture_iff_no_exotic theorem establishes that eliminating exotic representations is exactly equivalent to proving the formula conjecture.

sections.title: Concrete Non-Exotic Examples and the n=6 Case
sections.summary: Proves not_exotic for 4, 8, 9, 25 (prime powers). Shows n=6 has 2 prime factors and is not exotic (via conjecture axiom). buDimFormula_six = max(buDim 2, buDim 3).
sections.mathContext: n=6 is the smallest n with 2 distinct prime factors — the minimal case where exotic behavior would be novel. Under the conjecture, buDim(6,d) = max(buDim(2,d), buDim(3,d)).

conclusion.summary: Exotic representations — where composite groups exceed the prime factor formula — require n to have ≥ 2 distinct prime factors. Primes and prime powers are provably non-exotic. Under the formula conjecture, no exotic representations exist at all. The first potential exotic case would be n = 6.
conclusion.implications: The formal analysis shows exotic representations would be direct counterexamples to the Fadell-Husseini index formula for composite cyclic groups. The structural constraints (exotic requires ≥ 2 prime factors) narrow the search space. Proving non-existence for n = 6 (= 2 × 3) would require either the formula conjecture or a direct topological argument about Z/6-equivariant maps.
openQuestions: Can the non-existence of exotic representations be proved for n = 6 without invoking the formula conjecture axiom?
Does Bredon's Smith theory give a direct proof of non-exotic for p^k without the formula conjecture?
For n = pq (product of two primes), is there a direct proof that buDim(pq, d) = max(buDim(p,d), buDim(q,d))?
